scored_features.gate_reasoning: G1: 'iinjurytype' is listed among trial_measured_features so the feature is observed in the dataset. G2: The hypothesis explicitly invokes systemic hyperfibrinolysis vs focal surgical bleed (a named pathophysiological process) linking mechanism-of-injury to TXA pharmacodynamics. G3: This proposes a genuine PD effect-modification (blunt polytrauma → more hyperfibrinolysis → greater TXA responsiveness) rather than only an absolute-risk amplification. G4: There is conceptual and observational support linking mechanism-of-injury to fibrinolysis patterns but no robust RCT subgroup evidence showing a blunt-vs-penetrating × TXA interaction, so the specific interaction is not well-supported by trial literature. G4 FALSE — cascade: G5 also FALSE.
scored_features.justification: Decisive gate: G4 failed because while physiology and observational data link injury mechanism to fibrinolysis, there is insufficient RCT/subgroup evidence that blunt vs penetrating injury reliably modifies TXA effect in trials.

G2: The hypothesis specifies concrete biological distinctions (intracranial bleeding dynamics vs extracranial haemorrhage and differing responsiveness to systemic antifibrinolytics) that mechanistically connect ICC categories to TXA action. scored_features.justification: Decisive gate: G5 passed because ICC categories map to well-defined clinical groups (e.g., head injury vs extracranial bleeding) and there is trial evidence (CRASH-3) supporting differential TXA effects that can inform actionable decisions.

scored_features.justification: Decisive gate: G5 passed because time-to-treatment is a well-characterized, trial-supported, and operationally actionable modifier of TXA efficacy (e.g., CRASH-2 demonstrated the early-treatment benefit).
